name: builtins
description: Built-in stack operations, arithmetic, and control instructions.

instructions.name: dup
instructions.description: Copies the top value.

instructions.name: dup2
instructions.description: Copies the top two values.

instructions.name: swap
instructions.description: Exchanges the top two values.

instructions.name: over
instructions.description: Copies the second value to the top.

instructions.name: nip
instructions.description: Removes the second value.

instructions.name: drop
instructions.description: Removes the top value.

instructions.name: rot
instructions.description: Moves the third value to the top.

instructions.name: rrot
instructions.description: Moves the top value below the next two; the inverse of rot.

instructions.name: tuck
instructions.description: Copies the top value below the second.

instructions.name: drop2
instructions.description: Removes the top two values.

instructions.name: pick
instructions.signature: (x y z -- x y z x)
instructions.description: Copies the third value to the top.

instructions.name: call
instructions.description: Runs a function value: a fn { } literal, a local holding one, or &name.

instructions.name: dip
instructions.description: Runs q on what is under x, then puts x back.

instructions.name: keep
instructions.description: Runs q on x, then puts x back on top.

instructions.name: dip2
instructions.description: Runs q on what is under the top two values, then puts them back.

instructions.name: keep2
instructions.description: Runs q on the top two values, then puts them back on top.

instructions.name: bi
instructions.description: Runs p on x, then q on x again, each on what the last left.

instructions.name: tri
instructions.description: Runs p, q and r on x in turn, as bi runs two.

instructions.name: both
instructions.description: Runs q on x, then on y.

instructions.name: times
instructions.description: Runs q n times; it must leave the stack as it found it.

instructions.name: each
instructions.description: Runs q with each element, or character of a string, on top; it must leave the stack as it found it.

instructions.name: map
instructions.description: Returns a new array of what q leaves for each element.

instructions.name: filter
instructions.description: Returns a new array of the elements q leaves a true flag for.

instructions.name: fold
instructions.description: Runs q on the accumulator and each element, or character of a string, in turn, starting from acc.

instructions.name: any
instructions.description: Returns 1 if q leaves a true flag for any element, or character of a string, stopping at the first that does.

instructions.name: all
instructions.description: Returns 1 if q leaves a true flag for every element, or character of a string, stopping at the first that does not.

instructions.name: find
instructions.description: Returns the first element, or character of a string, q leaves a true flag for, and 1; or the zero of the element type, and 0.

instructions.name: index
instructions.description: Returns the position of the first element, or character of a string, q leaves a true flag for, or -1.

instructions.name: scan
instructions.description: Returns the position of the first element, or character of a string, at or after start that q leaves a true flag for, or -1.
Adds two numbers.
Subtracts b from a.
Multiplies two numbers.
Divides a by b.
Computes a modulo b.

instructions.name: neg
instructions.description: Negates a number.
Adds 1 to a number.
Subtracts 1 from a number.
Returns 1 if a equals b, 0 otherwise.
Returns 1 if a does not equal b, 0 otherwise.
Returns 1 if a is less than b, 0 otherwise.
Returns 1 if a is greater than b, 0 otherwise.
Returns 1 if a is less than or equal to b, 0 otherwise.
Returns 1 if a is greater than or equal to b, 0 otherwise.

instructions.name: within
instructions.description: Returns 1 if a is in [low, high], both ends included, 0 otherwise.

instructions.name: and
instructions.description: Returns 1 if both values are non-zero, 0 otherwise; both are always evaluated. `bits::and` is the bitwise one.

instructions.name: or
instructions.description: Returns 1 if either value is non-zero, 0 otherwise; both are always evaluated. `bits::or` is the bitwise one.

instructions.name: not
instructions.description: Returns 1 if the value is zero, 0 otherwise. `bits::not` is the bitwise ones' complement.

instructions.name: cast<T>
instructions.description: Converts x to T, written cast<T>: one of i64, f64, d128, ptr and str.

instructions.name: sizeof<T>
instructions.description: Returns the size of T in bytes, written sizeof<T>; known at compile time.

instructions.name: nth
instructions.description: Returns the element at index i; in a string, the character there, as its codepoint.

instructions.name: set
instructions.description: Stores x at index i.

instructions.name: len
instructions.description: Returns the number of elements in an array, or of characters in a string.

instructions.name: append
instructions.description: Appends x and returns the array, which may have moved.

instructions.name: print
instructions.description: Prints a value without a newline.

instructions.name: dump
instructions.description: Prints a value with its type, for debugging.

instructions.name: nl
instructions.description: Prints a newline.

instructions.name: free
instructions.description: Frees an array or a struct.

instructions.name: panic
instructions.description: Signals an error and returns from the fallible function.

instructions.name: err
instructions.description: Returns the message and code of the last failed call, and clears them.

instructions.name: ok
instructions.description: Returns 1 if a fallible call's status is Ok (0), and 0 if it is an error code.

instructions.name: fail
instructions.description: Returns 1 if a fallible call's status is an error code, and 0 if it is Ok.
